note: Declared gates for the release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml). Each tagged release candidate is re-evaluated from scratch on the dev and validation samples (never a held-out test) and compared with the committed score reports. Changing a tolerance is a change to this file, with its reason in the commit.
baseline: eval/reports/<sample>-score-hybrid-1-extents-derived.json and ...-sel2.json, committed and produced on the development machine (Apple M1, Metal)

rules_exact.rule: equal in every sample: the rules involve no model, so any difference is a code or data change

model_systems.rule: pooled over the six samples, no more than 3 records below the baseline. The baseline came from Metal on the development machine; the runner decodes on x86 CPU, where greedy outputs can differ for a few records

abstention.rule: pooled, no more than 3 records below the baseline

selection_2.rule: pooled over the six samples, hybrid-1 with selection-2 holds back at least twice as many wrong as correct ready regions, and its ready regions are no less precise than without it (the release default since 0.1.2)

quantization_parity.reference: release/manifest-q8.json (Q8_0, the same upstream revision and GGUF repository revision)
quantization_parity.metric: LLM-alone critical_exact_match rate, pooled over the six samples
quantization_parity.rule: the shipped quant loses no more than 1 percentage point against the reference, both run on the same runner type

reported_not_gated: model seconds per record (p50, p95) and the llama-server container's peak memory, for each quant. The GitHub runner is not the declared reference machine, so latency targets are not judged here.
